title: IIT/NEET Journey: The Ultimate Exam Prep
description: Every Indian student's ultimate challenge. Balance intense preparation, mental health, social life, and family expectations as you prepare for the most competitive exams in the world. Your choices over 6 crucial months determine your rank, your future, and who you become.

scenes.title: The Decision
scenes.narrative: Class 11 results are out. You scored well — top 10 in your school. The family is gathered around the dinner table. Daal, roti, and the weight of your entire future. Papa puts down his chai and looks at you. 'Beta, IIT ya NEET?' The eternal Indian family question. Dadi wants a doctor in the family. Chacha says engineers make more money. Your heart races. This single choice shapes the next 2 years of your life.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian family gathered around a dinner table in a middle-class home, parents looking expectantly at a teenage student, textbooks and report card on the table, warm yellow lighting from a tubelight, chai cups, Indian home decor with calendar on wall, emotional family moment, detailed illustration

choices.label: IIT — I want to be an engineer!
choices.description: The dream of every engineering aspirant. JEE Advanced awaits.

choices.label: NEET — Medicine is my calling
choices.description: The noble path of healing. NEET UG is your battlefield.

scenes.title: Choosing Your Path
scenes.narrative: JEE it is! Papa beams with pride. 'Mere bete ka IIT hoga!' Now the big question — which coaching institute? The billboards on every Kota street compete for your attention. Allen, FIITJEE, Resonance — the names you've heard since childhood. Your school friend Rahul has already joined one and sends you selfies from the Kota hostel. 'Bhai, yahan toh alag hi duniya hai.' The pressure is real, but so is the opportunity.
scenes.image_prompt: Busy street in Kota Rajasthan with massive coaching institute billboards and banners everywhere, students walking with heavy backpacks, auto-rickshaws, a teenage student looking up at the billboards with determination and slight nervousness, coaching center buildings in background, vibrant Indian city illustration

choices.label: Join the big coaching factory (Kota)
choices.description: Move to Kota for intensive coaching. Lakhs of students compete here every year.

choices.label: Self-study with online resources
choices.description: Stay home, use YouTube, Unacademy, PW, and your own discipline.

scenes.title: The Medical Path
scenes.narrative: NEET preparation begins. Mom tears up a little — 'Mere ghar mein doctor hoga!' Your biology teacher, Sharma Ma'am, thinks you have real potential. 'Tumhare conceptual understanding acche hain,' she says after class. The question is how to prepare. The pressure from family and peers is already building. Relatives call every week asking about your 'preparation.' The neighborhood aunty has already started telling people her beta is becoming a doctor.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian student sitting at a study desk with biology textbooks and NCERT books stacked high, anatomy chart on the wall, a supportive mother bringing chai, phone showing NEET preparation app, warm bedroom lighting with a desk lamp, motivational quotes pinned on soft board, detailed Indian home study room illustration

choices.label: Intensive coaching program
choices.description: Join a top NEET coaching institute. 6 hours of classes + 6 hours of self-study daily.

choices.label: Balanced approach with school + self-study
choices.description: Attend school, study at home, use selective coaching for weak subjects.

scenes.title: Month Zero
scenes.narrative: Your preparation officially begins tomorrow. Textbooks stacked on the desk — HC Verma, Irodov, NCERT, RD Sharma, MS Chouhan. Phone notifications silenced. A fresh study schedule pinned to the wall with colored markers. 6 months to the exam. 180 days. 4320 hours. Every single one counts. Your room transforms from a teenager's space into a war room. The only decoration left is a small photo of your dream college. Let's begin.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian student's study room transformed into an exam preparation war room, desk covered with HC Verma and NCERT textbooks, handwritten study timetable pinned on wall with colored markers, phone placed face down, a small photo of IIT/AIIMS campus pinned above desk, early morning light through window, determined expression, cinematic Indian student life illustration

npcs.name: Mishra Sir
npcs.personality: Strict but brilliant. Old-school teaching methods. Believes in 16-hour study days. Tough love approach. Speaks in a mix of Hindi and English. Known for his iconic dialogues.
npcs.backstory: 25 years of teaching experience. Has produced 50+ IIT toppers and 30+ AIIMS selections. Wakes up at 4 AM. Never takes a holiday during exam season. His own son is an IITian. Believes shortcuts don't work but smart work does. Famous for his line: 'Agar mehnat karte ho toh result aayega, guarantee meri.'

npcs.name: Rahul
npcs.personality: Your competitor and friend. Sometimes helpful, sometimes triggers toxic comparison. Shares notes but also brags about mock scores. Always online on WhatsApp study groups. Has a love-hate relationship with preparation.
npcs.backstory: Your classmate since 8th standard. Both of you dreamed of cracking the exam together. He joined coaching 6 months before you. Sometimes his mock scores make you anxious, sometimes his doubt-clearing sessions save your day. He deals with his own pressure by projecting confidence. Deep down, he's as scared as you are.

npcs.name: Mom
npcs.personality: Wants the best for you. Makes chai at midnight. Worries about your health. Sometimes adds pressure without realizing. Her love language is food and checking if you've eaten. Compares you to Sharma ji ka beta without meaning to hurt.
npcs.backstory: Sacrificed her own career aspirations so you could have the best opportunities. Works tirelessly to ensure you have everything you need. Stays up late making sure you've eaten. Her biggest fear is that the pressure will break you. She doesn't understand the syllabus but understands your moods better than anyone. When she says 'Sharma ji ka Priya ne toh...' she doesn't realize how much it stings.

competitors.name: Priya Sharma
competitors.chat_personality: The neighborhood genius everyone compares you to. Always tops mock tests. Annoyingly disciplined. Wakes up at 4 AM. Completes the syllabus before everyone else. Not arrogant, but her existence is enough to give you anxiety. Sharma ji brings her marks up in every family gathering.

base_rounds.title: Month 1 — The Foundation
base_rounds.story: First month of serious prep. The syllabus looks like Mount Everest — Physics, Chemistry, Maths/Biology, each with 20+ chapters. Your coaching teacher has assigned 200 problems this week alone. Friends are going to a movie this weekend. Your phone buzzes with Instagram reels of people having fun. The hostel room feels small. The study table feels enormous. This is where it begins.
base_rounds.goal: Establish a strong study foundation and routine
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian student surrounded by towering stacks of textbooks and coaching material at a small study desk, problem sheets scattered everywhere, phone showing Instagram notification, window showing friends leaving for movie outside, contrast between fun and study, warm desk lamp lighting, relatable Indian student life illustration

choices.label: Hardcore study mode — 12 hours/day
choices.description: Wake up at 5 AM, study till midnight. No entertainment. No social life. Just books.
choices.feedback: Incredible progress! You finished 3 chapters of Physics and 50 problems in Organic Chemistry. But you're already exhausted by day 20. Dark circles forming. Mishra Sir nods approvingly.

choices.label: Balanced schedule — 8 hours study, breaks included
choices.description: Study with Pomodoro technique. Take walks. Sleep 7 hours. Sustainable pace.
choices.feedback: Sustainable pace. You're fresh and learning effectively. Mom is happy you're eating properly. Rahul teases you for 'taking it easy' but you feel good about your retention.

choices.label: Focus on understanding concepts, not grinding
choices.description: Fewer problems, deeper understanding. Build intuition before speed.
choices.feedback: Deep understanding is building. When Mishra Sir asks a tricky conceptual question in class, you're the only one who answers correctly. 'Yeh ladka door tak jayega,' he tells the class. But practice count is low.

choices.label: Follow the topper's schedule from YouTube
choices.description: Copy the exact routine of last year's AIR 1. If it worked for them...

probability_outcomes.feedback: The topper's schedule actually works well for you! Structured approach helps organize your preparation. Lucky match with your learning style.
One size doesn't fit all. The topper studied 14 hours because that was THEIR capacity. You burnt out trying to match someone else's rhythm. Lesson learned the hard way.

choices.feedback: One size doesn't fit all...

base_rounds.title: Month 2 — The First Mock Test
base_rounds.story: First full-length mock test. 3 hours, 200 questions. Your hands are shaking as the timer starts. The OMR sheet looks intimidating. Rahul finished 30 minutes early and is grinning outside the hall. You're stuck on question 47 — a Thermodynamics problem that should be easy but your mind has gone blank. The clock ticks louder with every second.
base_rounds.goal: Complete your first mock test and learn from the results
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian student in an exam hall with OMR sheet and question paper, hand trembling slightly while holding a pencil, wall clock showing time pressure, other students bent over their papers, one student outside the window looking confident, tense examination atmosphere, detailed realistic illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: You panicked and couldn't finish! Only 60% attempted. The blank bubbles on the OMR sheet stare back at you accusingly. But hey — better to learn this now than on the real exam day.

choices.label: Attempt all questions, guess if needed
choices.description: No question left blank. Mark something for everything. Negative marking be damned.

probability_outcomes.feedback: Your educated guesses paid off more often than not! 65% accuracy on guessed questions. Sometimes fortune favors the bold.
Negative marking destroyed your score! You lost 30 marks on wrong guesses alone. Mishra Sir's words echo: 'Mock mein marks jaaye toh chalega, exam mein nahi.'

choices.feedback: Bold strategy. Negative marking is a risk...

choices.label: Focus on strong subjects, skip weak ones
choices.description: Maximize accuracy. Only attempt questions you're 80% sure about.
choices.feedback: Smart test strategy! 92% accuracy in attempted questions. Mishra Sir looks at your sheet and says 'Isko kehte hain samajhdaari.' You attempted 140/200 but scored higher than those who attempted all.

choices.label: Time yourself strictly — 1 min per question
choices.description: Strict time allocation. Move on if stuck. Circle and come back.
choices.feedback: Great time management! You finished with 10 minutes to spare and used them to review flagged questions. Three corrections in the review saved you 12 marks!

choices.label: Panic and leave after Section 1
choices.description: The anxiety is overwhelming. You can't think straight. Walk out.
choices.feedback: Anxiety took over. You sat in the corridor with your head in your hands. But Mishra Sir finds you and says something unexpected: 'At least you experienced it now, not on exam day. This is what mocks are for.' Mom makes your favorite aloo paratha when you get home.

base_rounds.title: Month 3 — The Comparison Trap
base_rounds.story: Rahul scored 180/300 in the mock. Sharma ji ka Priya got 230. You got 145. Your WhatsApp group is buzzing with screenshots of scores. Mom asks 'Rahul ne kitne aaye?' at dinner. Papa reads about toppers in the newspaper. The comparison monster is eating you alive. Every Instagram story from coaching friends shows their DPP scores. You lie awake at 2 AM wondering if you're good enough.
base_rounds.goal: Handle peer pressure and comparison while staying focused
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian student lying awake in bed at 2 AM looking at phone showing WhatsApp group messages with mock test scores, comparison and jealousy visible in expression, phone screen glow illuminating worried face, other students' scores highlighted, dark room with study materials visible, emotional and relatable illustration

choices.label: Delete social media, go monk mode
choices.description: Uninstall Instagram, mute WhatsApp groups. Complete digital detox.
choices.feedback: Digital detox! Focus skyrockets. You gain 2 extra hours daily that were wasted scrolling. The silence is uncomfortable at first but liberating by week 2. Rahul messages 'Bhai tu zinda hai?' You don't reply for 3 days.

choices.label: Use competition as motivation
choices.description: Channel the comparison energy into fuel. If they can score 230, so can you.
choices.feedback: Healthy competition pushes you harder. You solve 50 extra problems this week just to prove a point. When Rahul shares his next score, instead of anxiety you feel motivation. 'Next mock mein dekhna,' you tell yourself.

choices.label: Talk to Mom about the pressure
choices.description: Open up about how comparisons hurt. Be vulnerable with family.
choices.feedback: Mom listens quietly. Then she says: 'Beta, humne kabhi Sharma ji se compete nahi kiya. Apna best do, bas.' She stops asking about Rahul's marks. That night she makes gajar ka halwa and sits with you while you study. You feel lighter than you have in weeks.

choices.label: Change strategy — find a personal mentor
choices.description: Connect with a senior IITian/doctor who cracked the exam. Get personalized guidance.
choices.feedback: A senior IITian from your city starts guiding you personally. 'Mere time pe main 130 pe tha month 3 mein. Final mein 280 aaya,' they say. Suddenly your 145 doesn't look so bad. Their study plan is tailored just for you. Game changer.

base_rounds.title: Month 4 — The Burnout Wall
base_rounds.story: 4 months in. You've studied every single day. Dark circles have become permanent. Headaches every evening. The page in front of you is blurry — you read the same line 5 times and nothing registers. Mishra Sir says 'Yahi woh time hai jab toppers bante hain — push through!' Your body says otherwise. Mom notices you haven't laughed in weeks. Your handwriting in notes has become illegible. You fall asleep at the desk twice this week.
base_rounds.goal: Navigate burnout without destroying your preparation
base_rounds.image_prompt: Exhausted Indian student fallen asleep at study desk with face on open textbook, dark circles visible, empty chai cups and energy drink cans on desk, crumpled paper everywhere, motivational poster peeling off wall, early morning light suggesting all-night study, mother peeking through doorway with worried expression, emotional burnout illustration

choices.label: Push through — no breaks until exam
choices.description: Mishra Sir's way. Pain is temporary, rank is permanent. Keep grinding.
choices.feedback: You're grinding hard. Two more chapters completed. But at what cost? You snapped at Mom when she asked you to eat. You can't remember the last time you smiled. The knowledge is going in, but something inside is breaking.

choices.label: Take a 3-day complete break
choices.description: No books. Sleep 10 hours. Watch a movie. Go for a walk. Reset completely.
choices.feedback: You slept 12 hours the first day. Watched 3 Imtiaz Ali movies. Went for chaat with Mom. Came back on day 4 and the textbook made sense again. It felt like your brain defragmented itself. Mishra Sir disapproves but you don't care.

choices.label: Switch to active learning — teach others
choices.description: Start explaining concepts to weaker students. Teaching is the best revision.
choices.feedback: Teaching is the best way to learn! When you explain Organic Chemistry mechanisms to Rahul, your own concepts solidify. 'Bhai tu toh professor ban ja,' Rahul says. The change of pace refreshes you. Your WhatsApp study group starts calling you 'Sir.'

choices.label: Seek professional help for stress
choices.description: Visit a counselor or therapist. Mental health is health too.
choices.feedback: The school counselor teaches you breathing exercises and cognitive reframing. 'Your worth is not your rank,' she says. You learn that 60% of coaching students face similar burnout. It's not weakness — it's human. Brave and smart decision. Mom is proud of your maturity.

base_rounds.title: Month 5 — Revision Overdrive

ai_generation_context.context: Month 5 of IIT/NEET preparation. The student has been preparing for 5 months and needs to enter revision overdrive. The exam is 1 month away. Syllabus completion is the main worry. The player needs to decide how to prioritize revision vs new topics vs practice. Indian exam preparation context with coaching classes, mock tests, and family pressure.

base_rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant study room filled with books and colorful posters, a large desk cluttered with notes and laptops, sunlight streaming through the window, a sense of urgency in the air

base_rounds.title: The Weak Subject Problem
base_rounds.story: Mock test analysis reveals a devastating pattern: Physical Chemistry (or Biology Section B) is your Achilles heel. Consistently losing 40-50 marks here. You've been avoiding it because it's painful. But the data is clear — fixing this single weakness could jump your rank by thousands. Mishra Sir pulls you aside: 'Yeh subject tumhe niche kheech raha hai. 15 din do isko.' But 15 days is a lot when the exam is around the corner.
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian student analyzing mock test results on a score sheet with red marks highlighting weak subject areas, bar graphs showing subject-wise performance, Physical Chemistry or Biology textbook looking intimidating, coaching teacher pointing at the weak area on the sheet, analytical and strategic mood, Indian coaching center classroom illustration

choices.label: Intensive crash course on weak subject
choices.description: Two weeks of pure Physical Chemistry/Biology. Morning to night. Nothing else.
choices.feedback: Two weeks of pure Physical Chemistry/Biology. Painful but effective. You went from scoring 15/60 to 42/60 in that section. The improvement is dramatic. But other subjects got rusty during the neglect. Trade-offs, always trade-offs.

choices.label: Maximize strong subjects instead
choices.description: Why fix weaknesses when you can be exceptional at strengths? Score 100% where you're already good.
choices.feedback: Your strong subjects become ironclad. 95%+ accuracy in Maths/Physics (or Botany/Zoology). But the weak subject remains a bleeding wound. It's a strategic gamble — will the strengths compensate enough?

choices.label: Find a specialist tutor for that subject
choices.description: Hire a subject-specific tutor. One-on-one attention for your weak areas.
choices.feedback: The tutor — an ex-IITian who now teaches only Physical Chemistry — makes complex concepts click in days. 'Tumhe sirf perspective change karna tha,' they say. Electrochemistry suddenly makes sense. Money well spent.

choices.label: Previous year question analysis — targeted practice
choices.description: Study 10 years of previous papers. Find patterns. Practice only high-frequency topics.
choices.feedback: Patterns emerge! You realize 60% of questions come from just 8 chapters. Thermodynamics, Electrochemistry, Chemical Equilibrium — these repeat every year. You laser-focus on these. Smart work over hard work. Mishra Sir approves: 'Ab samajh aaya!'

base_rounds.title: D-Minus 7 — Final Week
base_rounds.story: One week left. The syllabus revision is incomplete — at least 3 chapters untouched. Sleep is luxury. Rahul says he's done 3 full revisions and is 'chilling now.' Your confidence wavers. The formula sheet you made is 47 pages long. Mom makes your favorite rajma chawal. Papa comes to your room, sits quietly for a minute, and says: 'Beta, hum tum par proud hain, result kuch bhi aaye.' Your admit card is pinned to the wall. The countdown begins.
base_rounds.goal: Make the most of the final crucial week before the exam
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian student in final week of exam prep with admit card pinned on wall, calendar showing exam date circled in red with X marks on passed days, formula sheets and revision notes spread across bed and desk, father standing at doorway with emotional expression, nervous but determined student, countdown timer feeling, intense Indian exam preparation illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Paralyzed by anxiety in the final week! You sat staring at your books unable to decide what to study. The most crucial week was wasted in indecision. But you still have exam day — trust what you've already learned.

choices.label: Power revision — 18 hour days
choices.description: Sleep 4 hours. Study the rest. Cover maximum syllabus. Last sprint.
choices.feedback: Superhuman effort. You covered 80% of the remaining syllabus. Red Bull and chai kept you going. But your hands are trembling and you can barely keep your eyes open. Is this sustainable till exam day?

choices.label: Focus on formulas and key concepts only
choices.description: High-yield revision. Important formulas, key theorems, frequent question types only.
choices.feedback: Strategic revision. You created a 5-page formula cheat sheet from the 47-page one. Key concepts reinforced. High-yield topics nailed. You didn't cover everything, but you perfected what matters most.

choices.label: Solve 5 full mock tests
choices.description: One mock per day. Simulate exam conditions. Analyze errors immediately after.
choices.feedback: Practice makes perfect. Your speed improves dramatically. By the 5th mock, you finish 15 minutes early. Error analysis reveals your silly mistake rate dropped from 12% to 4%. Exam simulation builds real confidence.

choices.label: Rest and preserve mental energy
choices.description: Light revision only. Sleep 8 hours. Eat well. Arrive at exam fresh and sharp.
choices.feedback: You arrive at the exam well-rested. Clear mind. While others have dark circles and trembling hands, you feel calm. Mom's rajma chawal and Papa's words carry you. Sometimes the best preparation in the last week is rest.

base_rounds.title: Exam Day
base_rounds.story: D-Day. 5:30 AM alarm. Mom has made poha and given you dahi-cheeni for luck. Papa drops you at the center on his scooter. 'All the best, beta.' You're sitting in the exam hall. Roll number checked. Admit card on the desk. Paper in hand. 3 hours on the clock. Heart pounding so loud you're sure the person next to you can hear it. The invigilator says 'You may begin.' You flip the first page. The first question is... surprisingly easy. Or is it a trap? This is everything you've worked for. 180 days compressed into 180 minutes.
base_rounds.goal: Perform your best on exam day
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian student sitting in a large examination hall on exam day, question paper just opened on desk, hundreds of students in rows, wall clock showing start of exam, invigilator walking between rows, mix of nervousness and determination on face, admit card visible on desk, bright institutional lighting, dramatic and emotional exam day illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Time ran out before you could attempt all sections! The invigilator's 'Time's up!' hits like a truck. You look at the 40 unattempted questions. Months of preparation and you couldn't manage 3 hours. The walk out of the hall is the longest walk of your life.

choices.label: Steady and systematic — follow your strategy
choices.description: Stick to the plan you practiced in mocks. Section by section. No panic.
choices.feedback: You stuck to your plan. Calm under pressure. Section 1 done in 50 minutes, Section 2 in 55, Section 3 in 50. Five minutes to review. You caught two silly mistakes in the review. Months of mock practice paid off. Well done.

choices.label: Start with easy questions for momentum
choices.description: Quick wins first. Build confidence. Then tackle the hard ones.
choices.feedback: Quick wins boost confidence! You nail 40 easy questions in the first 30 minutes. The momentum carries you through medium questions. By the time you hit the hard ones, you're in the zone. Adrenaline is your friend today.

choices.label: All-out aggressive — attempt everything
choices.description: Leave no question blank. Maximum attempts. Risk the negative marking.

probability_outcomes.feedback: Your aggressive approach paid off! The educated guesses landed more often than not. 190/200 attempted, 75% accuracy. The risk-taking gave you an edge over cautious test-takers.

Negative marking destroyed your score! You attempted everything but accuracy dropped to 55%. Lost 35 marks to wrong answers alone. The aggressive strategy backfired spectacularly. Rahul's strategic approach suddenly looks wise.

choices.feedback: Bold strategy. Negative marking is the question...

choices.label: Trust your gut and instincts
choices.description: Don't overthink. Let 6 months of preparation guide you naturally.
choices.feedback: You let your months of preparation guide you naturally. No clock-watching, no strategy sheets — just you and the paper. Surprisingly, the answers flow. Your subconscious knows more than you think. You walk out feeling peaceful, regardless of the result.

crisis_events.title: Syllabus Change Announcement!
crisis_events.description: Breaking News: NTA announces changes to the exam pattern! New chapter added, weightage shifted. 20% of your preparation focus is now on low-priority topics. WhatsApp groups are exploding. Coaching institutes are issuing emergency circulars. Everyone is panicking.

choices.label: Quickly adapt study plan
choices.description: Restructure your entire schedule to align with new pattern. Fast but stressful.
choices.feedback: You spent 2 days replanning everything. The new schedule is tighter but aligned with the updated pattern. Mishra Sir sends a revised DPP set. Adaptability is a skill too.

choices.label: Ignore and stick to current plan
choices.description: Don't panic. Fundamentals don't change. Trust your preparation.
choices.feedback: While everyone panics, you stay calm. The fundamentals haven't changed — just the packaging. Your deep conceptual understanding means the pattern change barely affects you. Smart students adapt; wise students don't need to.

crisis_events.title: Friend's Mental Health Crisis
crisis_events.description: Rahul calls you crying at 2 AM. His voice is broken. He's thinking of giving up everything. His parents have been fighting about money — the coaching fees are straining the family. 'Kya fayda hai bhai, main toh crack nahi kar paunga,' he sobs. He needs a friend right now. Your textbook is open to a chapter you must finish tonight.

choices.label: Spend the night talking to him
choices.description: Close the books. Be there for your friend. Some things matter more than marks.
choices.feedback: You talked until 5 AM. Rahul calmed down. You told him about your own struggles. 'Bhai, tera support na hota toh...' he says. You lost a night of study but gained something money can't buy. The next day, Rahul shows up to class with a small smile.

choices.label: Advise him to seek professional help
choices.description: You're not equipped to handle this. Guide him to a counselor.
choices.feedback: You spend 30 minutes convincing Rahul to talk to the school counselor. 'Bhai, yeh mera kaam nahi hai, but I know someone who can help better.' It feels cold, but it's the right call. Rahul sees the counselor the next day and starts feeling better with professional support.

crisis_events.title: Health Scare!
crisis_events.description: You faint during a mock test. The room spins and everything goes black. You wake up in the coaching center's first-aid room. Doctor diagnosis: severe Vitamin D and B12 deficiency, dehydration, and acute stress. 'Beta, 3 din complete rest. No negotiation,' the doctor says firmly. Mom is crying on the phone.

choices.label: Follow doctor's orders strictly
choices.description: 3 full days of rest. No books. Proper food. Sunlight. Supplements.
choices.feedback: Three days of sleep, mom's food, and actual sunlight. You forgot what the sun looked like. The doctor's supplements kick in by day 2. You return feeling like a different person. Health is the foundation everything else is built on.

choices.label: Rest 1 day, study light for 2
choices.description: Compromise. One day of complete rest, then light revision from bed.
choices.feedback: You can't help yourself — the NCERT is on your bedside table by evening of day 1. Light revision for 2 days. Not ideal but you covered some ground. The doctor shakes her head. Mom shakes her head. But at least you rested some.

crisis_events.title: Paper Leak Scare!
crisis_events.description: Viral WhatsApp forwards claim the exam paper has been leaked! Suspicious PDFs circulating in every coaching group. 'CONFIRMED LEAK — FORWARD TO ALL STUDENTS' messages flooding your phone. Some students are sharing and memorizing answers. Social media is on fire. News channels are debating. Your anxiety spikes.

choices.label: Ignore completely — focus on your prep
choices.description: It's probably fake. Even if real, NTA will handle it. Don't waste energy on this.
choices.feedback: You mute all groups and go back to your formula sheet. Smart move — it turns out to be a fake leak, as usual. Students who wasted hours on the fake PDF lost precious revision time. Your focus is your superpower.

choices.label: Report to authorities and move on
choices.description: Forward the suspicious content to NTA's helpline. Do your duty, then get back to studying.
choices.feedback: You report to NTA's anti-cheating helpline and post on their portal. Then you switch off your phone and study. NTA confirms it's fake within hours and thanks vigilant students. You did the right thing AND protected your study time.

interdependencies.message: Your mental health is severely impacting your ability to study! You read the same paragraph 10 times and nothing registers.
Strong knowledge base is boosting your exam confidence! You know your stuff and it shows.
Poor time management means fewer practice tests completed! You keep starting mocks but never finishing them.
Low confidence is causing silly mistakes in practice tests! Second-guessing yourself on questions you actually know.

Exam center list released. Students advised to visit centers a day before for route planning.

achievements.description: Achieve a legendary rank in the top 100. The dream of every aspirant realized.

achievements.title: Balanced Life
achievements.description: Maintain mental health while achieving strong knowledge. Proof that balance works.

achievements.title: Mock Test Champion
achievements.description: Dominate mock tests with an exceptional practice score.

achievements.title: Time Lord
achievements.description: Master the art of time management during preparation.

achievements.title: Never Give Up
achievements.description: Maintain mental strength and confidence throughout the journey.

achievements.title: Study Group Hero
achievements.description: Help others learn while strengthening your own knowledge.

achievements.description: Complete the exam journey with a respectable practice score.

endings.title: AIR Under 100 — Dream College!
endings.description: You did it! Your name appears on the toppers list. The website crashes from traffic but your roll number is RIGHT THERE. Tears of joy. Mom can't stop crying. Papa's chest swells with pride — he calls everyone in the family. Dadi does a puja. The newspaper wants your interview. IIT Bombay CSE / AIIMS Delhi — the dream is real. The sacrifices, the dark circles, the missed movies, the 2 AM chai sessions — every single second was worth it. 'Sharma ji ka beta toh...' For once, you ARE the Sharma ji ka beta story.

endings.title: Top 1000 — Excellent College
endings.description: Not AIR 1, but an amazing result. NIT Trichy, IIT Roorkee, or a top medical college — you earned your spot among the best. Your hard work paid off. The family celebrates with a dinner at your favorite restaurant. Papa orders dessert for the whole table. 'Mere beta ne kar dikhaya!' Mishra Sir texts: 'Proud of you. Ab college mein bhi mehnat karna.' A bright, brilliant future awaits.

endings.title: Good College — Solid Foundation
endings.description: You made it to a good college. Not the dream IIT/AIIMS, but a solid state NIT, IIIT, or a respected medical college. It's not what you imagined in your wildest dreams, but here's the secret nobody tells you: many of India's most successful people started exactly where you are. The college name opens a door, but what you do inside is what matters. Papa says: 'Sapne bade rakho, shuruat choti ho toh kya.' He's right.

endings.title: Gap Year — Try Again
endings.description: Not your year. The result stings. Mom says 'Koi nahi beta.' Papa is quiet — he's hiding his own disappointment to protect yours. But here's what you learned: 6 months of intense preparation taught you more about yourself than any exam could. You know your weak spots now. You know your mistakes. A gap year to prepare again. Remember — many toppers took 2 attempts. Some even 3. The journey isn't over. It's just a longer route to the same destination.

endings.title: Different Path — And That's OK
endings.description: The exam didn't go as planned. But somewhere during these 6 months, you discovered something unexpected about yourself. Maybe it was the way you explained concepts to Rahul. Maybe it was the study schedule design that worked beautifully. Maybe it was the realization that your passion lies elsewhere — design, business, writing, arts. India has a million paths to success, and IIT/NEET is just one of them. Sundar Pichai took time to find his path too. Your chapter is just beginning.

endings.title: Burnout — The Cost of Pressure
endings.description: The pressure was too much. Your health suffered — physically and mentally. The exam became secondary to surviving each day. You're not alone in this: thousands of students face this every year. The system failed you, not the other way around. But healing comes first. Take time. Breathe. Talk to someone. The exam will be there next year. Your health and happiness cannot wait. As the counselor said: 'You are more than a rank. You always were.'

random_events.text: School declares an unexpected holiday for a local festival! An entire bonus day to study without coaching classes. You use it to clear doubts in Organic Chemistry that had been piling up.

6-hour power cut in the middle of summer. No fan, no light, no internet. The inverter dies in 2 hours. You try studying by candlelight like the toppers in motivational videos but it's not romantic at all — it's just hot and miserable.

A motivational video about a student from a small town cracking IIT with AIR 50 goes viral. Their story mirrors yours in many ways. 'Agar woh kar sakta hai, toh main bhi,' you think. Sometimes inspiration comes from the most unexpected places.

how_to_play: You are an Indian student preparing for the most competitive exam of your life — IIT JEE or NEET. Every decision over 6 months affects your Knowledge Level, Mental Health, Practice Score, Time Management, and Confidence.
Talk to NPCs for guidance — Mishra Sir for study strategy, Rahul for peer support, and Mom for emotional strength. Build trust with them through your choices.
Some rounds are timed! Quick decisions required — just like in the real exam. Hesitation has consequences.
Watch for crisis events that appear randomly — syllabus changes, health scares, and paper leak rumors. How you handle pressure defines your journey.
Balance is key: pushing too hard damages mental health, but too much rest means falling behind. Find your own rhythm.
learning_objectives: Understand the importance of balanced preparation over pure grinding in competitive exam prep.
Learn to manage stress, peer pressure, and family expectations during high-pressure academic periods.
Develop strategic thinking about time management, subject prioritization, and test-taking techniques.
Recognize the signs of burnout and understand the value of mental health in academic performance.
Appreciate that exam results, while important, do not define your entire future or self-worth.

glossary_terms.definition: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — your fallback if no deal is reached.
glossary_terms.example: If you can't agree on a price, you could sell to a different buyer — that's your BATNA.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: A strong BATNA gives negotiating power. Knowing both parties' BATNAs reveals who needs the deal more.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: A job applicant with another offer has a stronger BATNA and can negotiate more confidently.

glossary_terms.definition: Finding solutions where both parties gain value rather than one side winning at the other's expense.
glossary_terms.example: Agreeing on a payment plan that works for both buyer and seller, rather than a discount that hurts profit.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Integrative negotiation expands the 'pie' by identifying trade-offs where each party values things differently.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Labor-management negotiations that increase productivity in exchange for better wages can benefit both sides.

glossary_terms.definition: Setting an initial reference point in a negotiation that influences the final outcome.
glossary_terms.example: The first price mentioned in a negotiation becomes the anchor around which all counteroffers are compared.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research shows people are heavily influenced by the first number they hear, even when irrelevant.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Salary negotiations: starting with a high number tends to result in higher final offers.

coaching_moment: Understand the importance of balanced preparation over pure grinding in competitive exam prep. Learn to manage stress, peer pressure, and family expectations during high-pressure academic periods.
cultural_context: The JEE and NEET examinations are among the most competitive in the world, with over 2 million candidates each year competing for limited seats. This game models the real psychological journey of preparation — developing the resilience and delayed gratification that define successful candidates.
reflection_prompt: How did you adapt as the AI shifted strategies? Which adaptation worked best?
